articles.title: Buying a Refurbished PS5 Is Your Best Bet for a More Affordable Way to Play GTA 6 This November
articles.summary: Looking for a more affordable way to play GTA 6 this November? Here is why buying a certified refurbished PS5 is your best bet to save money on hardware right now.
body: If you're staring at the price of a new PS5 and wondering whether playing GTA 6 this November is really worth $600 or more, I'd strongly recommend looking at refurbished consoles before you do anything else.

There's simply not much value in paying full price for a brand-new PS5 right now. Sony's current pricing puts the PS5 Digital Edition at $599.99 and the disc-drive model at $649.99, while the PS5 Pro costs a frankly ridiculous $899.99.

That's a lot of money to spend if GTA 6 is the main reason you're finally jumping into the current generation. Thankfully, a reputable refurbished console can knock a meaningful chunk off that price without having to wait around for a potential price cut over Black Friday.
My first stop right now would be PlayStation Direct, where Sony is selling certified refurbished PS5 consoles directly through its own store.

articles.title: Saber Boss Reacts To The Death Of Physical Games And Rising Console Prices
articles.summary: 2026 has been full of big storylines in gaming, including Sony's announcement that it will end support for physical PlayStation game discs in 2028 and the trend of consoles getting increasingly expensive.
body: He said he was "surprised how upset people were" about Sony ending support for physical game discs. Willits said he hasn't bought a physical game "in a long time" because he enjoys the convenience of digital games. Willits is not alone, as the share of digital game sales is growing at numerous companies.

At the same time, Sony continues to sell millions of physical game discs annually. Willits said Saber still makes "a lot of money" from physical games, especially in Europe, but the trends are different in North America, he observed.

Willits went on to say he had an interaction with someone recently who asked him to sign a copy of Doom 3, a game he worked on when he was with id Software. "So for me personally, I'll miss that in the future," he said.
Part of what many people enjoy about physical games is collecting the boxes they come in and presenting them on their shelves.

articles.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Battle Royale-Inspired PvP Mode Where You Can Strip The Flesh Off Enemies
articles.summary: Gears of War games have had some of the best multiplayer action around ever since the days of the first game, and for Gears of War: E-Day, developers at The Coalition are looking to give fans plenty of options for online fun.
body: "It's very obviously inspired by battle royale games, but it's on a Gear-sized PVP map," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "At the beginning of the map, there's lots of mobility, teams are moving around, you're trading the Power Core back and forth. But as the map goes on, you see defensive teams start to build up a front around the player they're protecting. And then, in awesome Gears fashion, the thing you're going to hold puts you at a slight disadvantage. So we gave you a heavy weapon that's basically a giant battery pack, and if somebody gets close to you within a really tight range, you can strip all the flesh off their body with a charge attack."

Crucible is one of four PvP modes that will be available on launch day. The multiplayer options include traditional Team Deathmatch, Conquest, and Demolition, each of which has been reworked for E-Day. Team Deathmatch has a dynamic respawn system to move spawn locations closer to where fights are breaking out, Conquest puts its own spin on the classic King of the Hill experience, and Demolition revolves around teams planting bombs on enemy territory.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Is Making Major Upgrades to Both Ends of the Court
articles.summary: Let's be honest, the NBA offseason has already thrown up enough plot twists to fill a MyCAREER cutscene. LeBron James scooting off to Philly, the Lakers embroiled in an ownership drama involving a reported $12.5 billion valuation, and Victor Wembanyama going from basketball's terrifyingly talented…
body: Fortunately, there's a new NBA 2K on the way to keep me occupied. After the franchise's big preseason reveal dropped details across virtually every mode, here's my vibe check on what my fellow hoopers should be psyched for most.

NBA 2K27 is making a pretty convincing case that this year's biggest changes aren't about finding one overpowered move and spamming it until my opponent rage-quits. The offensive side of the ball gets new toys including step-through up-and-unders, a Dynamic Layup Engine and expanded dribbling customisation, giving me more control over how I create space and attack the rim.

Defence isn't parking its arse on the bench either. Hands-up defence has been redesigned, the shot contest system has been overhauled, defensive cutoffs have been expanded and a new collision system should give physical play more weight. In other words, NBA 2K27 is trying to make both ends of the court count, which sounds like good news for anyone who has ever watched a teammate sprint towards the three-point line and decide defence is somebody else's problem.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto III – The Legacy Review
articles.summary: Replaying the pioneering 2001 classic 25 years later and paying tribute to the game that didn’t just change the trajectory of the GTA series forever – it changed the business.
body: Over the next few months, I’m going to be taking a look back at each of the core Grand Theft Auto games and replaying them in the lead-up to the arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. What we’ll be putting together won’t be traditional re-reviews, and they won’t come with any new IGN score, but they will re-examine what made each GTA remarkable upon the time of its release. By the end of the project, using GTA’s previously six-star wanted level, you should be able to get an idea of where each of these games roughly rank in my long-term love for this series.
Today, we go back to the game that changed this series forever: Grand Theft Auto III.

It’s true that its already annoying targeting system is doubly frustrating by modern standards, and its time-consuming mission restarts do feel particularly punitive 25 years on. However, I’ve found it impossible not to admire how well it otherwise weaves together its driving, action, story, and exploration within a dynamic 3D world, considering it accomplished this before there was any sort of proper blueprint for doing so. Sure, GTA III didn’t get everything right immediately – but you’ve got to walk before you can run.
points: Replaying the pioneering 2001 classic 25 years later and paying tribute to the game that didn’t just change the trajectory of the GTA series forever – it changed the business.

articles.title: Saber Responds To AI Criticisms In Rideshare Game And Promises, “We Will Never Fire Someone And Replace Them With AI”
articles.summary: One of the biggest talking points in gaming today is the use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has.
body: Now, Saber's chief creative officer, Tim Willits, has addressed the situation as well, promising that, "We will never fire someone and replace them with AI."

For anyone just catching up, Rideshare Stimulator is an upcoming Saber game where players take on the role of an Uber- or Lyft-like driver and interact with them as they take them to their location. The developers freely admit to using generative AI in various capacities, and now Willits has shed more light on the situation. He said the game's main campaign features dialogue written by humans, but there is also a "free ride" mode where Rideshare Stimulator wants to be able to reference current events in the real world.
"We use AI to generate that because we want to do it so fast," Willits said, adding that the plan is for weekly or biweekly updates with this kind of AI-generated content.

Willits also clarified that some of Saber's other games, including the new Hellraiser, Turok, Stuntman, and Space Marine games, also do not use AI. Saber, like many other game companies, is experimenting with AI in various ways.

It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has.

articles.title: After GTA 6: Extended Look Showed Rockstar's Game Running at 30FPS, Tech Experts Say a 60FPS Console Version Is 'Extremely Unlikely' and 'Genuinely Challenging' Even on PC
articles.summary: Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.
body: Yesterday's 27-minute reveal featured 30fps footage of the game on Netflix, YouTube, and in the raw file made available by Rockstar to download — and this is seemingly how we should all expect the game to look when it arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S this November.

While 30fps might seem low compared to the frame counts of other modern gaming blockbusters, Rockstar appears to be targeting this level to maximize the sheer detail on offer in every one of those frames, Digital Foundry believes.

"It's clear that the focus was absolutely maximising the level of visual detail at a fixed 30fps frame-rate on all platforms," Digital Foundry wrote in an Extended Look deep dive article. "The rendering, simulation and presentation have all been tuned around that constraint - and the result is an unprecedented level of density, material quality and world coherence, with trade-offs landing primarily in image quality and animation smoothness rather than systemic scale or fidelity."

articles.title: Hellraiser: Revival Is More Than Just Cenobites and Gore – 10 Things We Learned From Saber Interactive
articles.summary: October wouldn't feel right without a spooky game or two, and Hellraiser: Revival is shaping up to be a terrifying-- and horny --dive into the nightmarish fiction of author Clive Barker.
body: Hellraiser: Revival launches for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 6.

The legendary creator of Hellraiser needed some convincing before he started collaborating with Saber Interactive, but once he was assured that the developers had a grasp of the Hellraiser franchise, he gave the studio the freedom to tell their own tale within that dark universe. "Clive Barker was such a permissive partner to work with," narrative director Anthony De Fault said. "He was really supportive of our ideas. He basically just wanted to make sure we understood Hellraiser as a franchise, and then, once he knew that we had the, we were channeling the same spirit that he was channeling back in the '80s, he just let us go."

articles.title: Hell Let Loose: Vietnam review
articles.summary: The most surprising thing about Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is how much DNA it shares with Big Walk. They both frequently involve traversing large expanses of terrain. They both have excellent maps. Most of all, they're both fundamentally games about communication.
body: The difference is in how they encourage chatty players. Big Walk gently coaxes players out of their shells through the medium of ingenious puzzles and good vibes. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam forces you to chat with your random squadmates because if you don't you're going to get bombed to shit. Where Big Walk is all carrot, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is all stick, and it will not hesitate to thwack you with it if you don't play by the rules.

Grappling with Hell Let Loose: Vietnam can be an intimidating experience. But while its teaching style is much harsher, it does yield rewards. When Hell Let Loose: Vietnam comes together—with dozens of players working in tandem to overcome the enemy—the resulting show is utterly captivating. Unfortunately, it doesn't come together quite often enough to justify the pain of getting to that point.
points: The most surprising thing about Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is how much DNA it shares with Big Walk.

articles.title: Resident Evil 4 Remake ‘Chapter 0’ Released to Bring Back Cut Content
articles.summary: Capcom’s Resident Evil 4 remake took a fairly ambitious approach to updating this classic. The game reworked several sequences, toned down the original’s escort mission woes, and added the ability to parry a chainsaw, which was quite neat.
body: It seems the remake was originally supposed to have even more Ashley-specific segments. Data miners found evidence of a scrapped prologue chapter which follows Ashley as she flees from her pursuers the night before Leon arrives in the village. While Capcom never completed the sequence, a modder combined the leftover pieces of this "Chapter 0" with existing in-game assets to create a playable version available on NexusMods.

In the mod, Ashley uses her phone as a flashlight while navigating the village at night. After witnessing the cultists murder an outsider, she also sees Luis being captured. The modder provides a detailed breakdown of what was restored, recreated, and added from the game files. Essentially, most of the animations, camera angles, and unique features, like Ashley’s phone flashlight, were from the game’s files. Everything else was stitched together from existing assets. The mod seamlessly integrates the prologue to play after the game’s opening cutscene and before Chapter 1.
points: Capcom’s Resident Evil 4 remake took a fairly ambitious approach to updating this classic.
The game reworked several sequences, toned down the original’s escort mission woes, and added the ability to parry a chainsaw, which was quite neat.

articles.title: Xbox's New Fable Hones the Classic Series' Combat to Near-Perfection
articles.summary: At Gamescom, Polygon had the opportunity to play a 30-minute Fable demo behind closed doors. It was focused solely on combat: An early game quest took me, alongside a dry-witted character named Humphry, through an abandoned mine full of undead skeletons and wraiths, followed by a misty bog that…
body: It’s no wonder Playground Games has been so keen to showcase its role-playing game’s combat, because it is unbelievably fluid. Before I went hands-on, one of the devs explained that the team’s goal was to make combat as seamless as possible across melee, ranged, and magic, so the three blend together as one. Playground nailed it.

Melee weapons, as you’d expect, have the usual light or heavy options, with combos available for repeated swings. Your bow can be used to take out foes from afar, but you can also equip a repeater crossbow, which is much better for crowd control. And then there are the spells: from an antigravity suspension spell that lifts enemies into the air, to the offense-focused targeted lightning bolt or fireball, you can switch between them on the fly.

Fable isn’t about creating a character build that specializes in one type of combat or another, because you’re the hero, and that means you can do anything. When in combat, melee attacks are on the face buttons, aiming and firing the bow are on the triggers, and if you want to switch to magic, just hold the right trigger when not aiming and press the face buttons to cast a spell.

articles.title: Rockstar says GTA 6 runs at 30 FPS, while it's reportedly unsure about a 60 FPS performance mode
articles.summary: UPDATE 3.30PM BST: Performance perfectionist Digital Foundry has scrutinised the latest GTA 6 trailer ( which can be downloaded for a closer, purer appraisal) and said that on this evidence it looks like GTA 6 is running at 1440p natively on PS5 and maintains "a relatively stable and well-paced 30…
body: ORIGINAL STORY 2.20 BST: We've had our extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 - did you notice? - and one of the reactions I saw from readers during our live report was about frame-rate. In short, some people said it looked noticeably low. Perhaps that's to be expected given it was captured on a base PS5, but it does raise the bigger question of what frame-rate GTA 6 runs at on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, how that might change for the PS5 Pro, and whether it offers optional Performance and Quality modes for any of those platforms.

The answer, according to Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson, is 30 FPS - that's what he told Portuguese outlet Flow Games reporter Davy Jones (via GamesRadar+ ). But the situation regarding a 60 FPS option, which is usually the Performance mode, is less clear.

"According to the director, it is still necessary to consult the technical team to determine if there will be a 60 FPS option at launch (or in the future)," Flow Games reported (translated via Google). "He also emphasises that he does not currently have details on resolution and other technical qualities, such as the use of Ray Tracing, but the performance, for now, is 30 FPS."

articles.title: DC Officially Unveils New Superman Replacement
articles.summary: Superman is the biggest character in comics, the default superhero for many in a world that has thousands upon thousands. The character has appeared in nearly a dozen live-action films, countless more animated projects, and virtually infinite comic books as he works to spread his message of good.
body: As such, there have also been countless different versions of the Last Son of Krypton from the iconic Superman Blue to Ultraman, Kal-L, Kingdom Come version, and beyond. The latest iteration, however, may be the Man of Steel's most terrifying yet.

The new Superman appears in Next Level: One Shot #1, a new special from writer Gerry Duggan, artist Fernando Blanco, and letterer Buddy Beaudoin. The book follows Deadshot, real name Floyd Lawton, as he uncovers a haunting conspiracy involving genetically engineered copies of the most powerful people in the DC Universe, including Superman himself.

Although he appears alongside cloned versions of Wonder Woman and Batman, Superman is the one that instantly stands out — largely because of just how haunting he really is. As Supes himself explains, this version of the clone had to have his eyes removed because "previous iterations of me with complete bodies were too dangerous."

articles.title: "Somebody will make the Half-Life 2 of AI" - after the Rideshare controversy, Saber CCO says something will come along and "change people's minds" about gen-AI
articles.summary: Saber Interactive made headlines recently when its boss had an ugly spat with a former employee about the company's use of gen-AI in taxi game Rideshare Stimulator. Matthew Karch, Saber's co-founder and CEO, since apologised, and made sure Rideshare got proper AI disclosure labels on Steam.
body: Saber is a large video game developer and publisher with 15 studios around the world, responsible for games like the acclaimed Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2. Its roster of upcoming games includes a new big-budget John Wick action game, a new Stuntman driving game, a new Turok game, a Hellraiser game, a Jurassic Park survival game, and the Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake. So the decision whether to adopt gen-AI more widely affects many more games than Rideshare.

With this in mind, Eurogamer's Connor sat down with Saber's chief creative officer Tim Willits - formerly of id Software - at Gamescom. As Willits put it to Eurogamer: "We are experimenting with it. A game we announced called Rideshare - it's a small game - we're going to try to figure out if it works or if it doesn't work. We don't as an industry really know how it fits, and consumers don't really know what they want or they don't want, so it's kind of like a disruptive technology that society has seen for a long time."
He then clarified: "We don't actually use it on our projects except for our experiment with Rideshare. We don't have an official policy; we don't use it outright across all our projects."
points: Saber Interactive made headlines recently when its boss had an ugly spat with a former employee about the company's use of gen-AI in taxi game Rideshare Stimulator.

Fable launches February 23, 2027. Pre-Order to receive the Pre-Order Content Pack, featuring the questionably heroic Chicken Suit and a collection of charming in-game gifts.

points: The world of Grand Theft Auto 6 is bustling and full of life.
Past GTA games are well known for how reactive NPCs in the open world can be to the player's actions.
In GTA 6, that all gets dialed up to 11 with major changes to not just the NPCs around you, but with certain design elements in the…
In this video, we talk about our time at Rockstar and what we've learned about how Grand Theft Auto 6's open world has changed dramatically to immerse the player like never before.
